topic: CNY/USD used to express CNY fee caps
why: Bank tariffs are denominated in CNY. Only the CNY 100 / 500 / 120 caps are affected; at 400,000 USD the whole cap swing is under 15 USD (IRS 2025 avg = 7.129; Fed H.10 noon buying rate 2026-11-06 = 6.6760). No rate forecast is used anywhere.

topic: FX spread on a bank wire
why: No published executable CNY/USD customer quote was obtained for any account, so a band is modelled instead of a number. This is the single largest cost component and must be replaced by the bank's own executable quote before acting.

topic: FX spread on cash / counter conversion
why: Banknote spreads are wider than telegraphic spreads; no published cash quote was obtained.

topic: FX spread on card / ATM settlement
why: Card scheme settlement rates and issuer foreign-transaction fees vary; none was verified for this account.
Offshore spreads are narrower in normal conditions; eligibility for an individual to move RMB offshore was not verified (see F05).

topic: Fixed fees at banks other than HSBC China
value: same as the HSBC China published tariff
why: Only one itemised personal tariff (S06) was verified. Other banks publish different tariffs; substitute your own bank's schedule.
No per-transfer ceiling for a non-domestic individual remittance was verified, so the model does not invent one. If your bank splits a large remittance, multiply the fixed fee.
Preparer fees for FBAR / Form 8938 / Form 1116 vary by provider and were not verified. Filing itself has no fee. The exposure is the penalty for not filing.

topic: PRC tax actually payable on the balance
why: Tax depends on the character of the underlying income and on what was already withheld. The ladder shows statutory rates and marks the resulting cell as exposure, not a bill.
